newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BROTHER OF N.Y. YANKEES MANAGER GETS HEART.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BROTHER OF N.Y. YANKEES MANAGER GETS HEART.

text.p: The brother of New York Yankees manager Joe Torre underwent a four-hour heart transplant operation on Friday and should be well enough to listen to the sixth game of the World Series, a hospital spokesman said.
Frank Torre, 64, has been in New York's Columbia Presbyterian Medical Centre since August, suffering from heart disease and waiting for a new heart.
"He watched the Yanks 1-0 victory over the Braves in Atlanta last night, and he was very pleased," said hospital spokesman Bob deLuna. "At 3 a.m., he was notified that a new heart had been found."
Eric Rose, one of the heart surgeons who operated on Torre, said: "We expect that he will be fully awake by Saturday in time for the game."
Asked if it would be safe for Torre to watch what could be a nail-biting game, Rose said: "He's much better off watching the game with a new heart than with his old heart."
The Yankees lead the best-of-seven-games World Series, three victories to two. Game Six is scheduled for Saturday night at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx.
Surgeon Mehmet Oz said Torre's condition was critical but stable. "It was one of the smoothest heart transplants we've performed at the hospital," he said.
The organ came from a 28-year-old New York City man.
Torre played with the Milwaukee Braves in two World Series against the Yankees. In 1957, the Braves upset the Yankees and the next year lost to them.
